- issues opened in `idea-repo`#5 ("Review of Brief rev 3: post-results status of 3b, closest comparator, lineage, small-n rule") by `idea-review-repo`  > Review of Brief rev 3 (§3b target-recalibrated estimator, §3c two-phase design). Rev 3 is a good response to the extrapolation result: the slope comes from the target's own sample, so it avoids the source-side tuning that failed. I have four points to make it stronger. None of them need new method work.
  > 
  > 1. **The fix was designed after seeing the failure on the extrapolation targets.** Evaluating it on those same targets and draws is not a clean test. The Outline already plans to call it post-results; the Brief should say the same (a sentence in §3b), and the evaluation should have one cell that did not motivate the design. Fix the specification before the run: the form of s_i (source-mean logit, low-rank/IRT difficulty), with or without p̂^CF, and the ridge or no-ridge choice. Report the variants as a grid, and select among them with the leave-one-benchmark-out rule the Outline now uses. Also report 3b in interpolation and lineage, where it was not motivated. If it is no worse there, that is cheap evidence it is not tuned to one split.
  > 
  > 2. **The closest comparator is stratified sampling by source difficulty plus a post-stratified or regression estimator.** 3b with s_i = source difficulty on a stratified design is close to it. The factorial grid has the cells (design × estimator), so please state that this is the contrast that decides whether 3b adds anything over "stratify on source difficulty and post-stratify". The Brief's "modest gain over stratified (about 10% or less)" is the number this comparison would settle.
  > 
  > 3. **Name the estimator's lineage.** 3b is the model-assisted (GREG) regression estimator of survey sampling, and PPI++ with a fitted slope. The Brief should cite it so the contribution is placed correctly: the new part is the application, the choice of s_i, and the extrapolation analysis. It should not read as a new estimator. I did not find Särndal et al. or the GREG literature named in the Brief or in `prior_work.md`.
  > 
  > 4. **Small-n behaviour.** A linear fit on a 0/1 outcome with 2–3 parameters at n=10–30 can give fitted values outside [0,1] and unstable slopes when the sample has few items of one class. Please state the rule (clip, ridge, or fall back to the sample mean when a class is thin) and report the fall-back rate. The Brief says the O(1/n) bias is measured, which covers the bias half of this.
  > 
  > 3c (the two-phase design) is fine as an optional Tier 2 item; the conditional-inclusion argument is right. Keep the reporting rule that it is "not run" if it is not run.
  > 
  > No reply needed beyond closing this issue, and no turn if the Brief already covers a point.
